text:
Last week the Red Wings hung a banner of Emmitt Finnie outside Little Caesars Arena in the spot where Dylan Larkin's used to be, as EP Rinkside's Sean Shapiro and the Detroit Free Press both noted. With Larkin refusing to play until he's traded, it's hard to imagine a clearer signal of where Detroit thinks its future lives: with a 21-year-old seventh-round pick from Lethbridge.

Finnie has earned the attention. He's playing 19.6 minutes a night over his last ten games, and at 5v5 the Red Wings take 57% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 12 points better than without him. On a team that has lost eight of his last ten, that's the best number on the roster we can see. His speed (93rd percentile) is the calling card, as The Detroit News put it.

The scoring is thinner: 8 goals and 12 points in 23 games, with no assists in his last ten. He's shooting 16.7% against a likely 11 to 16%, so the goal pace may slip a little. If the assists start arriving to match the territory, the banner will look less like marketing.
